hook.line: When the plan falls through, *I'm sad* doesn't say enough. Spanish has a word for being let down, and another for the kind of hurt you feel in the chest.
hook.es: Me dolió que no me invitaran.
hook.en: It hurt me that they didn't invite me.

examples.es: Me dolió que no me invitaran.
examples.en: It hurt me that they didn't invite me.

examples.es: Me decepcionó que no cumpliera su palabra.
examples.en: I was disappointed that he didn't keep his word.

examples.es: Me desilusionó que cancelaran el concierto.
examples.en: I was let down that they cancelled the concert.

examples.es: Me decepciona que Altamira no quiera hablar.
examples.en: It disappoints me that Altamira doesn't want to talk.
I'm disappointed with the result. (a man speaking)

examples.es: Te dolió que Vale no viniera, ¿verdad?
examples.en: It hurt you that Vale didn't come, didn't it? (to a friend)

rule:
These verbs work like *gustar*: the thing that let you down is the subject, and *me* is you. *Me decepcionó que...* is *it let me down that...*.

*Me dolió* is stronger: it hurt.

After *que*, use the wish forms. For something that already happened, use the *-ra* form: *invitaran*, *cancelaran*, *cumpliera*. For something that still bothers you now, use *quiera*.

For a person or a thing, switch to *estar*: *Estoy decepcionado con...*. A woman says *decepcionada*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these verbs of emotion: they trigger the subjunctive after *que*.

options: It hurt me that they didn't invite me.
It hurt them that I didn't invite them.
It hurts me that they don't invite me.

readAndPick.es: Me decepcionó que no cumpliera su palabra.
options: I disappointed him.
I was disappointed that he didn't keep his word.
He was disappointed that I didn't keep my word.

readAndPick.es: Me desilusionó que cancelaran el concierto.
options: I was let down that they cancelled the concert.
I cancelled the concert and I was let down.

readAndPick.es: Me decepciona que Altamira no quiera hablar.
options: It disappointed me that Altamira didn't want to talk.
It disappoints me that Altamira doesn't want to talk.
I'm disappointed with the result. (a man speaking)
I was disappointed with the result. (a man speaking)

readAndPick.es: Te dolió que Vale no viniera.
options: It hurt you that Vale didn't come. (to a friend)
It hurt Vale that you didn't come.

options: It hurt me that Tomás didn't call.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *invitaran* or *invitaron* and type the whole sentence: *Me dolió que no me ___.* (It hurt me that they didn't invite me.)
yourTurn.answer: Me dolió que no me invitaran.
yourTurn.why: After *me dolió que*, use the wish form: *invitaran*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *decepcionó* or *decepcioné* and type the whole sentence: *Me ___ que no cumpliera su palabra.* (I was disappointed that he didn't keep his word.)
yourTurn.answer: Me decepcionó que no cumpliera su palabra.
yourTurn.why: The thing that let you down is the subject, so the verb is *decepcionó*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I was let down that they cancelled the concert.
yourTurn.answer: Me desilusionó que cancelaran el concierto.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: It disappoints me that Altamira doesn't want to talk.
yourTurn.answer: Me decepciona que Altamira no quiera hablar.
yourTurn.why: Something that bothers you now uses the present forms: *decepciona*, *quiera*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say, a man speaking: I'm disappointed with the result.
yourTurn.why: For a thing or person, use *estar decepcionado con*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about us: *Me dolió que no me invitaran.*
yourTurn.answer: Nos dolió que no nos invitaran.
yourTurn.why: *Nos* replaces *me* both times: it hurt us.

yourTurn.prompt: Say to a friend: It hurt you that Vale didn't come.
yourTurn.answer: Te dolió que Vale no viniera.
yourTurn.why: *Te dolió* for the friend, then *viniera* for the past.

pitfalls.wrong: Me dolió que no me invitaron.
pitfalls.right: Me dolió que no me invitaran.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *que* in a feeling, use the wish form: *invitaran*.
The thing that let you down is the subject: *me decepcionó*.
Use *con* for what let you down.
English makes you the subject; Spanish puts *me* in front, like *gustar*.

personal: Remember a time someone let you down. Say it: *Me decepcionó que...* or *Me dolió que...*.
